name: verified-absence
description: Verified absence counts (OPF-SPEC §3.5.8, §3.12.2, issue #251): evidence.absence has one record for every signed deal and clause type with no signed text, split into absent_verified and possibly_present, and the digest counts them per clause (n_signed_without_verified, n_signed_without_possible) and lists the verified deals (verified_absent_deals, latest signed_on first, undated last). The records are the output of the reference scorer over the deals' signed-text nodes: every node of a signed copy not filed under the clause is counted in n_checked, and a node filed under the clause that is too short to be precedent scores 1.0. Two clauses (assignment, governing law), eight deals. deal-a signed both clauses and is counted by neither; deal-g has no executed copy and is in no count. Assignment: deal-b (one node examined, its governing law clause, nothing close), deal-c (seven unclassified passages, none close), deal-f (opened with our standard and struck it before signing: it still signed without the clause; one node examined, its governing law clause) and deal-h (three nodes) are verified absent (n_signed_without_verified 4); deal-d has an unclassified passage scoring 0.308 against the clause and a passage the classifier filed under a third clause type (subcontracting) scoring 0.133 (a missed classification, so possibly present, candidates best first, each saying what the classifier filed it under, filed_under) and deal-e's executed copy yielded no nodes at all (basis unverifiable, possibly present, nothing checked): n_signed_without_possible 2. Governing law: deal-c and deal-d (whose five nodes score below the guard for this clause) are verified absent, ordered latest signed_on first (deal-d's month-only 2025-04 is after deal-c's 2025-03-10); deal-e is unverifiable and deal-h has a node the classifier assigned to the clause that was too short to be precedent (score 1.0, filed_under the clause itself), so possibly present. A node filed under the clause that is long enough to be precedent gives its deal a signed text and no absence record, so no record here cites one. The guard (0.1) is carried in evidence.absence.guard; a candidate scores at least that, and a scored record is absent_verified exactly when it has no candidate.

part_map.=: our part is present with the same legal effect
part_map.+: our part is present but more protective for perspective.party
part_map.-: our part is present but less protective for perspective.party
part_map.x+: our part is omitted, which is more protective for perspective.party
part_map.x-: our part is omitted, which is less protective for perspective.party
part_map.x0: our part is omitted with no effect on perspective.party

additions.+: an addition no part covers, more protective for perspective.party
additions.-: an addition no part covers, less protective for perspective.party
additions.0: an addition no part covers, neutral for perspective.party

label_by.parts: the default, so a digest entry omits label_by: the label is derived from the part map and additions; reason is the judgment's most important difference
label_by.owner: the owner set the label over the judged part map and additions, which may imply another label; reason is the owner's and wins

settled.agreed: an independent blind check reached the same label and parts as the judgment
settled.adjudicated: the blind check disagreed and a fresh agent decided: the judgment shown is that decision, so this label was contested and deserves more scrutiny
settled.unchecked: no completed blind check (none yet, or a disagreement still awaiting adjudication): weaker evidence than agreed or adjudicated
settled.owner: the owner set or corrected the judgment; it is never blind-checked
